name: quality-gate-swift
summary: A pre-commit gate for Swift projects: 45 SwiftSyntax-based checkers for recursion, pointer escape, concurrency, safety, documentation and release readiness, with SARIF output for GitHub Code Scanning. No overrides.
outcome: v3.2.1 runs 3,213 tests across 60 test targets and holds every project I ship at zero warnings and zero failures.

name: SwiftMCPServer
summary: A Swift 6 framework for building Model Context Protocol servers. The foundation under GeoSEOMCP, BusinessMathMCP and the production servers on roseclub.org.
outcome: 195/195 on the official conformance suite's 2026-07-28 requirements and 227/227 on the full suite, reproducible from the README.

name: SwiftMCPClient
summary: The client half of the Swift MCP ecosystem: HTTP/SSE, Streamable HTTP, WebSocket and stdio transports, OAuth, and MCPExplorer, a macOS app for poking at servers.
outcome: v0.12.0 ships its own conformance suite for stateless servers, run against SwiftMCPServer so the two halves are held to the same contract.

name: swift-oauth
summary: OAuth 2.1 for Swift, both sides: an authorization server and a client, with a conformance suite so another implementation can be held to the same rules.
outcome: v1.0.0-beta.5: 469 tests, gate 0/0, Linux CI green. Eight beta defects came from one real consumer and none from the test suite, which is why the 1.0 promotion waits on consumers.

name: GeoSEOMCP
summary: An MCP server that scores a website's visibility to AI systems: citability, structured data, crawler access, readability and brand authority.
outcome: 29 tools, 183 tests across domain, registration and contract suites; deployed in production behind geo-audit.

name: geo-audit
summary: A SaaS audit service for small businesses: Vapor, PostgreSQL, Redis job queues and Stripe, calling GeoSEOMCP for scoring.
outcome: A paid product built end to end by one person, from the spec through the systemd unit, on the same gate as the libraries beneath it.

name: BusinessMath
summary: Financial modeling, simulation and optimization in Swift 6: DCF, Monte Carlo, Black-Scholes, CDS pricing, efficient frontier, GPU-accelerated portfolio optimization.
outcome: The library behind BusinessMathMCP, which exposes 200+ of its calculations to AI assistants; a 12-week course on the site walks through it.

name: Shop Marriott
role: Head of Product, Hotels at Home
summary: Marriott's global online retailer of hotel home goods. One of 70+ storefronts across 40+ hospitality brands on a shared platform.
outcome: Re-platformed the front and back end across all 70+ sites with a 14-person global team, and used an LLM pipeline to harmonize 14,000 SKUs in four languages in about two hours for under $5.

name: Shop With Golf
summary: NBC Golf's content-and-commerce marketplace, pairing young golf brands with the network's coverage.
outcome: Took over a stalled $10mm project and launched in eight months with 29 brands. A Swift middleware prototype I wrote cut vendor onboarding from four months to two weeks.

name: Seeso
summary: NBCUniversal's subscription comedy streaming service, its first direct-to-consumer platform.
outcome: Appointed to lead retention: a RICE-prioritized program cut monthly churn by 6% in one quarter and lifted customer lifetime value by 40%. Shipped the Apple TV app in time for the holidays after the original vendor failed.

name: WineTaster 3
summary: Statistical analysis of blind wine tastings for iPhone, iPad and Apple Vision Pro, a modern successor to a DOS program by a former Princeton economics chair.
outcome: On the App Store; a native visionOS build shipped on Vision Pro launch day. The statistics package it needed was open-sourced and grew into BusinessMath.

name: Princeton 2000 Reunions
summary: The Class of 2000's 25th Reunion site, built and run for a 30-volunteer committee.
outcome: A record 2,000-person, $1mm+ reunion; the class leads all classes in annual giving dollars ($6.5mm) and participation (62.9%).

name: UCBComedy.com
role: Director of New Media and Development
summary: The Upright Citizens Brigade's third stage, created in 2008.
outcome: Developed and launched the site; produced 50+ digital shorts from a pool of 300 performers and 2,000 students.

name: Nassau Weekly
outcome: Conceived, designed and shipped the online edition in three weeks as a junior; grew advertising revenue 200% with a staff of 48.
